----------

**Welcome back!** OpenAI pointed its own model at its own plumbing and came out with a price cut, and Google taught robots to use their legs. Meanwhile Amazon booked $53 billion from owning a piece of Anthropic while Meta spent almost every dollar it earned and watched its stock fall.

**In today's Generative AI Newsletter:**

* **OpenAI:** Who actually found the savings behind the price cut?

* **Google:** What can its robots do that they couldn't last week?

* **Amazon:** Which investment made it more than its own business?

* **Meta:** Why did Wall Street punish a 28% revenue jump?


----------



----------
## ChatGPT made itself cheaper

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/50625ca6-1b9e-47f1-990e-f4253c745e13/Beehiiv_01_-_Jul_31.png?t=1785489739)
Caption: 

OpenAI [cut the price of GPT-5.6 Luna ](https://openai.com/index/advancing-the-price-performance-frontier-with-gpt-5-6/)by 80% yesterday, from $1 per million input tokens down to 20 cents. Terra came down 20%.

Your subscription price didn't move. What changed is that Luna and Terra now eat fewer credits inside Codex and ChatGPT Work, so the same plan stretches further.

Here's who found the savings. Inside a human-led process, GPT-5.6 Sol rewrote and optimized OpenAI's production kernels, then designed and ran hundreds of experiments on token generation.

That work cut the cost of serving the model by 20% and improved token-generation efficiency by more than 15%. OpenAI turned it into a price cut the next day.

Luna is the one to watch. On professional work it beats Fable 5 at an estimated cost per task nearly 99% lower, and runs year-ago frontier performance at roughly 6 cents on the dollar.

Replit's president called it the closest anyone has come to intelligence too cheap to meter.

Sol got Fast mode instead, 2.5 times quicker at double the price.

Five things happened this week. Each one changes how AI- and blockchain-driven companies operate, spend, and manage risk. Here is what every operator, founder, and investor needs to know. ◆ DEVELOPMENT 01 - Alphabet just had its worst trading day in over a year, and it was self-inflicted . Alphabet shares fell more than 7% after the company raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance to as much as $205 billion and reported negative free cash flow for the first time since its 2004 IPO. Meta dropped nearly 10% the same week on the same worry: AI infrastructure spending is now eating into cash generation faster than the market wants to tolerate. Together, Alphabet, Microsoft, Amazon and Meta are projected to spend roughly $724 billion on capex this year, and analysts expect that to approach $950 billion in 2027. Why it matters: the unwritten deal between investors and Big Tech spend whatever you want on AI as long as revenue keeps climbing just broke. The Ment Tech perspective: we help clients model AI infrastructure spend against actual revenue timelines before committing, so the build-vs-buy decision holds up under exactly this kind of investor scrutiny. ◆ DEVELOPMENT 02 - Apple did nothing, and it's now worth more than almost anyone else on Earth While its Magnificent Seven peers got punished for AI capex, Apple's stock climbed 15% in July alone and its market cap crossed $5 trillion, putting it alongside Nvidia as one of only two companies to hit that mark. Apple's strategy has been to avoid heavy in-house AI infrastructure spending and instead partner with outside model developers to power its services. Why it matters: the market just rewarded restraint over ambition, for the first time in this entire AI cycle. The Ment Tech perspective: not every client needs to own the infrastructure to win with AI. We build partnership-first architectures for clients who want AI capability without the balance-sheet risk that comes with owning the compute. ◆ DEVELOPMENT 03- Chip stocks just had their worst month since 2022 The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX) is down 17% in July after being up 101% in the first half of the year, on pace for its worst month since June 2022. Welcome to our July newsletter! This month, we take a look at the latest developments across the Volkswagen Group, from electric mobility and software innovation to future technologies and business results. From the world premiere of the Volkswagen ID. Cross, completing the Electric Urban Car Family, to new software capabilities powering our latest electric vehicles, July demonstrates how the Group is making advanced mobility accessible to more customers. At the same time, progress in autonomous driving, sustainable manufacturing and our battery ecosystem showcases the breadth of innovation across the Group. We also share updates on our latest delivery figures and half-year results. 🔍 Explore the 8️⃣ highlights that shaped this month: 🎉 1. World Premiere: ID. Cross The new Volkswagen ID. Cross celebrates its world premiere, completing the Electric Urban Car Family. 🗨️ Oliver Blume, CEO Volkswagen Group: "Four models, three brands, one platform: with the ID. Polo, the CUPRA Raval, the Škoda Epiq and the ID. Cross, Volkswagen Group is bringing individuality, quality and advanced technology to affordable electric mobility - without compromise." The strong customer response already shows the appeal of this concept: more than 54,000 orders have been received for the Electric Urban Car Family before all four models have even reached customers. 💻 2. Software Facts across the Electric Urban Car Family The Volkswagen Group's Electric Urban Car Family combines affordable electric mobility with a new software generation. Across models such as the CUPRA Raval, Volkswagen ID. Polo, Škoda Auto Epiq, and the Volkswagen ID. Cross, drivers benefit from features like Digital Key, next-generation Travel Assist, Android-based infotainment, connected vehicle services, and unique digital experiences tailored to everyday mobility. 🚗 3. Gen.Urban - Driving Experience in Urban Areas Volkswagen Group Innovation's self-driving research vehicle Gen.Urban has been collecting insights into future shared mobility in real-world traffic since the end of 2025. The project explores how passengers experience autonomous driving, which digital features best support work, entertainment, and relaxation and how-vehicle-passenger interaction should be designed. 🎨 4.
